config.title: Component Library Theming

intro.title: Component Library Theming
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a themed component library in Angular by creating a reusable button component that can change its appearance using custom properties. You will learn how to use Angular's @Input decorator to pass theme data from a parent component to a child component, allowing for dynamic styling. The main technologies involved are Angular components, TypeScript, and CSS custom properties for theming. By the end, you'll understand how to create flexible, themeable UI components that can adapt to different design systems.
intro.usecase: Component theming is essential for creating consistent, branded interfaces across enterprise applications. In real-world Angular projects, you'll implement theming systems for admin dashboards where different user roles need distinct color schemes, or e-commerce platforms requiring holiday-themed UI variations. Developers use these patterns to build design systems that maintain visual consistency across components like data tables, modals, and navigation menus while allowing quick rebranding. This approach enables teams to efficiently support multiple client brands or dark/light mode preferences without rewriting component styles.

objectives: Configure a theme service to manage color schemes across components
Apply CSS custom properties to style Angular components dynamically
Construct a theme toggle component that switches between light and dark modes
Bind component styles to theme variables for consistent theming
Integrate theme context into multiple library components
Manipulate theme properties programmatically based on user interactions
Render components with different themes to verify visual consistency

steps.title: Import Angular core modules and theming utilities
steps.instruction: Import Component and OnInit from '@angular/core' to create an Angular component.
steps.hint: Use the import statement with curly braces to import multiple symbols from the same module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing core Angular modules
import { Component, OnInit } from '@angular/core';
steps.expectedOutcome: The Angular core modules are imported, enabling component creation and lifecycle hooks.
successCriteria: Component and OnInit are imported from '@angular/core'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to import both Component and OnInit from '@angular/core'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check your import statement. You need to import Component and OnInit from '@angular/core'.

steps.title: Create the main ThemeProvider component
steps.instruction: Create a component class named ThemeProvider that implements OnInit and includes an empty ngOnInit method.
steps.hint: Use the @Component decorator with an empty selector and template for now. Remember to export the class.

seedCode.App.tsx:
import { Component, OnInit } from '@angular/core';

// Create the ThemeProvider component class here

steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a ThemeProvider component class with basic structure ready for adding theme logic.
successCriteria: ThemeProvider component class is defined with @Component decorator and implements OnInit.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've defined a class named ThemeProvider with @Component decorator and implements OnInit.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component structure isn't quite right. Check that you've created a ThemeProvider class with proper Angular component syntax.

steps.title: Define the Theme interface
steps.instruction: Create a TypeScript interface named 'Theme' with properties for 'primaryColor' (string) and 'spacing' (number).
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and define the properties with their types.
steps.expectedOutcome: A Theme interface is defined with the required properties, enabling type-safe theming.
successCriteria: The Theme interface exists with 'primaryColor: string' and 'spacing: number' properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the interface needs both properties: primaryColor (string) and spacing (number).
steps.feedbackWrong: The Theme interface is not correctly defined. Remember to use the 'interface' keyword and specify both property types.

steps.title: Initialize theme state with default values
steps.instruction: Inside the ThemeProvider component class, create a property called 'defaultTheme' that implements the Theme interface with sample values.
steps.hint: Define a property with type 'Theme' and assign it an object literal containing the required properties from the interface.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ThemeProvider component now has a defaultTheme property with initial theme values.
successCriteria: The defaultTheme property is defined with type 'Theme' and contains valid values for primaryColor, secondaryColor, and fontFamily.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure defaultTheme has all the required properties from the Theme interface with valid string values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The defaultTheme property should be defined with the Theme type and contain values for primaryColor, secondaryColor, and fontFamily.

steps.title: Create theme state property in component
steps.instruction: Inside the ThemeProviderComponent class, add a public property named 'theme' with type 'Theme' and assign it the 'defaultTheme' object you'll create.
steps.hint: Add a property declaration in the class body, like 'theme: Theme = defaultTheme;'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has a 'theme' property initialized with the default theme values, making the theme state available within the component.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a property, but check: does it have the correct type 'Theme' and is it assigned to 'defaultTheme'?
steps.feedbackWrong: The component should have a public property named 'theme' with type 'Theme' that's set to 'defaultTheme'. Review the example and try again.

steps.title: Define theme toggle handler
steps.instruction: In the ThemeProviderComponent class, add a method named toggleTheme that switches between a light theme and a dark theme by updating the theme property.
steps.hint: Define a method inside the class that changes the theme property values. You can create two theme objects (light and dark) and toggle between them.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a toggleTheme method that can switch the theme between light and dark variants.
successCriteria: A toggleTheme method is defined in the ThemeProviderComponent class that updates the theme property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your toggleTheme method actually updates the theme property with new values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The toggleTheme method is missing or doesn't properly update the theme property. Check the method definition and ensure it modifies the theme state.

steps.title: Set up component template structure
steps.instruction: Add a main container div element to the component's template.
steps.hint: In Angular, the template is defined in the @Component decorator. Add a div element inside the template string.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template now contains a main container div element.
successCriteria: The template property contains a div element
The template string is no longer empty
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added a div element inside the template string.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template should contain a div element. Check that you've added it inside the template property.

steps.hint: Use double curly braces {{ }} to bind the theme.primaryColor property in the paragraph text.
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will show a section with a heading and a paragraph displaying the current primary color value from the theme state.

steps.title: Add themed component demo
steps.instruction: Inside the template of your ThemeProviderComponent, add a <div> element that demonstrates theme usage by applying inline styles using the current theme values.
steps.hint: Use Angular's style binding syntax [style.property] to apply theme colors and font family to the div.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of applying theme styles in Angular
Themed content
steps.expectedOutcome: The template should now include a styled div element that visually demonstrates the current theme values.
successCriteria: A div element is added to the template with style bindings for background-color, color, and font-family using the theme properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a div, but make sure it uses all three theme properties (primaryColor, secondaryColor, fontFamily) with Angular style binding syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: The themed demo component isn't properly implemented. Check that you've added a div with style bindings to the theme properties.

steps.title: Add theme toggle button
steps.instruction: In the component's template, add a button element with the text 'Toggle Theme' that calls the toggleTheme method when clicked.
steps.hint: Use Angular's event binding syntax (click)="toggleTheme()" on a button element.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a click handler to a button in Angular
<button (click)="handleClick()">Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will contain a button that triggers the theme toggle functionality when clicked.
successCriteria: A button element with text 'Toggle Theme' is added to the template with (click)="toggleTheme()" event binding.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a button, but check if it has the correct text and click handler.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button is missing or doesn't have the correct structure. Make sure to add a button with 'Toggle Theme' text and (click)="toggleTheme()".

steps.title: Implement dynamic theme switching
steps.instruction: In the ThemeProviderComponent, implement the toggleTheme method to switch between a light theme and a dark theme by updating the theme property.
steps.hint: Inside the toggleTheme method, set this.theme to a different theme object. You can create a darkTheme object with different color values.
steps.expectedOutcome: The toggleTheme method will contain logic to switch between two different theme configurations.
successCriteria: The toggleTheme method updates the theme property to a different theme object (e.g., dark theme).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started implementing toggleTheme, but it doesn't fully switch between themes. Make sure you're updating this.theme to a complete theme object with different values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The toggleTheme method isn't implemented yet. Add logic inside the method to switch between two different theme configurations.

steps.title: Add theme context documentation
steps.instruction: Add JSDoc comments to the Theme interface and toggleTheme method to document their purpose and usage.
steps.hint: Use /** ... */ style comments above the interface and method to describe what they represent and how they should be used.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Theme interface and toggleTheme method will have clear documentation explaining their role in the theming system.
successCriteria: Theme interface has JSDoc comment describing what it represents, and toggleTheme method has JSDoc comment explaining its purpose.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some documentation, but make sure both the Theme interface and toggleTheme method have proper JSDoc comments describing their purpose and usage.
steps.feedbackWrong: The documentation is missing or incomplete. Add JSDoc comments (/** ... */) above both the Theme interface and toggleTheme method to document their purpose in the theming system.
